opus.w: The section only appropriates money and gives the act's short title ("Second Supplemental Appropriation Act, 1967"). No one outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision. There is no rulemaking, public hearing, advisory committee, consultation with states or tribes, or right to sue. Treating an appropriations decision as participation fails because the definition requires a process that brings outside parties in, and none exists here.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** You could argue that an appropriations act is a federal decision, so any process behind it might count as participation. That reading fails. This text is only the enacting clause of a supplemental appropriations act. It names no outside party and sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.
